# parity-fuzz --mode stat baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode stat --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (four seeds).
#
# Covers the zsh/stat module (c:Src/Modules/stat.c bin_stat). C's flag set is
# `g l L n N o r s t T` plus `A H f F`; the vocabulary had `A F H L n s` and now
# also generates the display flags `-o` (octal mode), `-r` (raw value + symbolic
# form), `-t` (always prefix the element name), `-T` (never prefix), and `-N`
# (never show the file name). Also covers `-A` array / `-H` hash destinations,
# `-F` time format, `-L` lstat on a symlink, whole-stat (no field selector), and
# the no-such-file / bad-option / no-such-element error paths.
#
# The vocabulary audit against C found NO bug — the module is faithful,
# including the parts most likely to drift: `-o` octal formatting, `-r`'s
# combined `33188 (-rw-r--r--)`, the `-t`/`-T` name prefix, symbolic `-s` mode,
# and the byte-exact `bad option: -%c` / `no such stat element` diagnostics.
#
# The display flags are restricted to +mode / +nlink because those are
# deterministic for a fixed fixture file; +size / +*time / +inode / +device vary
# and are only used through -A/-H/plain reads where the same file is stat'd by
# both shells so they still agree.
#
# The audit is recorded so this mode is not re-audited from scratch; a clean
# ungated flag is an untested one, and these are now generated.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
